headline: Jensen Beach flood recovery meeting planned as residents continue cleanup
subhead: Officials are planning a question-and-answer session as flooded households seek aid and answers about drainage.
teaser: A meeting with county, state and federal officials is planned for Jensen Beach flood survivors as cleanup continues. The meeting time and location have not been confirmed.
body:
A meeting with county, state and federal officials is being planned for Jensen Beach residents seeking answers about recent flooding and assistance with recovery. Stephen Leighton, chief of staff for U.S. Rep. Brian Mast, said residents would have an opportunity to raise questions about the flooding and available help during the week of November 16.

Leighton described the gathering as a question-and-answer town meeting during a [WPTV report on neighborhood recovery](https://www.wflx.com/2026/11/16/jensen-beach-neighbors-help-families-rebuild-weeks-after-historic-flooding/). A confirmed meeting time and location were not provided in that report. Residents should check with organizers before traveling to a meeting.

The planned discussion comes as volunteers, community organizations and neighbors continue helping families remove water-damaged belongings, drywall and other debris from flooded houses. Some residents face extensive repair bills, and others have questioned what help may be available to households without flood insurance.

Leighton said Florida had taken steps toward an emergency declaration and contacted the Federal Emergency Management Agency. Those steps do not, by themselves, mean federal individual disaster assistance has been approved. Residents are looking for clearer guidance on what aid may be available and how to seek it.

Another subject residents want addressed is how water moved through the Savannas Preserve and whether pumping from communities to the north contributed to flooding in Jensen Beach neighborhoods. County officials have discussed drainage and future flood prevention, but questions about the causes and responsibilities remain part of the public discussion.

For now, the cleanup continues. Residents and volunteers are helping families clear damaged homes, pack belongings and prepare for repairs. The planned meeting would give affected households an opportunity to ask government representatives about the next steps.

For the personal impact on one Jensen Beach household, read TCT's [account of Lisa and Jeremy French's effort to find housing and rebuild](https://treasurecoast.today/articles/2026-11-11-jensen-beach-family-seeks-housing-and-repair-funding-after-flooding-destroys-hom.html).
